findings.title: A keyspace that fails USE every time now makes the pool impossible to refill
findings.claim: A keyspace that fails USE every time now makes the pool impossible to refill. For example, a failed `Session::use_keyspace("typo")` leaves the bad keyspace set in every refiller, and the PR then discards every new connection instead of keeping it as before.

findings.title: The commit that balances total_connections when clearing pools leaves out a sibling drop…
findings.claim: The commit that balances total_connections when clearing pools leaves out a sibling drop path. An excess shard-aware connection in the `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` branch is dropped without dec_total_connections, even though count_in_metrics already incremented the metric for it.

findings.title: The keyspace check now runs before reshard and shard-aware port processing
findings.claim: The keyspace check now runs before reshard and shard-aware port processing. That is a silent behavior change not mentioned in the commit subject: sharder and shard-aware port updates, and advanced-shard-awareness mismatch detection, are deferred until a USE round trip completes.

findings.title: All four commits are subject-only with no body explaining why, yet the PR checklist…
findings.claim: All four commits are subject-only with no body explaining why, yet the PR checklist claims 'The commit messages explain what changes and why'.

findings.title: All four commits have a subject only and no body
findings.claim: All four commits have a subject only and no body. The PR checklist claims that 'The commit messages explain what changes and why', which is not true for the metrics-balance or keyspace-discard rationale.

findings.title: Commit 617139df is a fixup for a test added in 0d91aa54
findings.claim: Commit 617139df is a fixup for a test added in 0d91aa54. It replaces a yield_now busy-wait with a sleep instead of being squashed, so 0d91aa54 on its own carries the busy-waiting test.

findings.title: The per-connection keyspace failure log was downgraded from warn
findings.claim: The per-connection keyspace failure log was downgraded from warn! to debug!, so the now-fatal discard of a connection is invisible at default log levels.

findings.title: Comments still say ready_connections carries only connections whose keyspace was…
findings.claim: Comments still say ready_connections carries only connections whose keyspace was 'correctly set', and that a connection sent for keyspace setup will be 'finally put into the conns'. Both are now false.

findings.title: The test `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` does not prove a refill is triggered
findings.claim: The test `keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill` does not prove a refill is triggered. It calls handle_ready_connection directly with a hand-built error and checks only `need_filling()`. It never runs the refiller loop or the real producer, and it uses an error variant and event shape the production USE path never emits.

findings.title: `keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state` waits on `ready_connections
findings.claim: `keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state` waits on `ready_connections.next().await` without a timeout, and the USE future it awaits has no timeout either.

findings.title: The new keyspace tests break module conventions
findings.claim: The new keyspace tests break module conventions. They omit `setup_tracing()`, which every other test in the module calls. One of them also finishes the proxy before dropping the refiller, the reverse of the sibling tests, and so has to whitelist `DriverDisconnected`.

findings.title: The new tests copy the OPTIONS→SUPPORTED / STARTUP→READY proxy rules instead of reusing…
findings.claim: The new tests copy the OPTIONS→SUPPORTED / STARTUP→READY proxy rules instead of reusing or parameterizing start_simulated_node. There are now three more copies: make_rules in keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state and two rule vectors in resharding_discards_old_connections_and_balances_metrics. One of those copies also re-adds SCYLLA_SHARD_AWARE_PORT exactly as start_simulated_node does.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections calls dec_total_connections in a per-unit loop instead of…
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections calls dec_total_connections in a per-unit loop instead of using a bulk metrics operation.

findings.title: The two new keyspace tests do not call setup_tracing(), although CONTRIBUTING says any…
findings.claim: The two new keyspace tests do not call setup_tracing(), although CONTRIBUTING says any new test should. The other new tests in the same change do call it.

findings.title: Metric decrement responsibility is now spread across five hand-written sites with two…
findings.claim: Metric decrement responsibility is now spread across five hand-written sites with two different idioms: direct self.metrics.dec_total_connections() (keyspace arm, remove_connection) and decrement_total_connections(n), which callers must pair with a separate .clear() (run loop, excess limit, maybe_reshard). The helper takes a count instead of owning the clear.

findings.title: The private ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace variant and the new public…
findings.claim: The private ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace variant and the new public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant both represent the same keyspace-setup failure. The private enum exists only to route a classifier, and its name nearly collides with the existing ConnectionSetupRequestError.

findings.title: The Keyspace error arm copies the `if
findings.claim: The Keyspace error arm copies the `if !self.is_filling() && self.is_empty() { self.update_shared_conns(Some(err)) }` guard from the non-shard-aware Connection arm, but without the explanatory comment and with different backoff/flag semantics. Two parallel arms now each own the 'report error when pool is empty' rule.

findings.title: The new ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError message 'Failed to set keyspace while…
findings.claim: The new ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError message 'Failed to set keyspace while initializing a connection: {0}' diverges from the sibling UseKeyspaceError #[from] variants in errors.rs, which all use "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}".

findings.title: The unit-test fixture builds a keyspace-failure event that production can never produce
findings.claim: The unit-test fixture builds a keyspace-failure event that production can never produce. Real Keyspace errors always carry keyspace_name: Some(..) from start_setting_keyspace_for_connection, but the test passes keyspace_name: None. It also uses UseKeyspaceError::RequestTimeout, which this path cannot yield because the per-connection USE has no timeout (TODO at 1336).

findings.title: The keyspace tests build PoolRefiller by hand twice, copying mock_pool_refiller with a…
findings.claim: The keyspace tests build PoolRefiller by hand twice, copying mock_pool_refiller with a different reconnect-policy constructor. The new proxy rule sets also re-copy the OPTIONS/STARTUP rules from start_simulated_node.

findings.title: The new helper unrequested_connection_event is gated on #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] even…
findings.claim: The new helper unrequested_connection_event is gated on #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] even though nothing about it is metrics-specific. As a result, the non-metrics keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state test hand-builds the same OpenedConnectionEvent { result: Ok(open_connection(..)), requested_shard: None, keyspace_name: None } three times.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state hard-codes a raw CQL RESULT/SetKeyspace…
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state hard-codes a raw CQL RESULT/SetKeyspace frame body (kind 0x0003, u16 length 0x0008, "keyspace"). That body must stay byte-for-byte in sync with the separate VerifiedKeyspaceName::new("keyspace") literal used later in the same test.

findings.title: The fix commit is titled 'avoid busy-waiting in metrics test', but…
findings.claim: The fix commit is titled 'avoid busy-waiting in metrics test', but full_pool_clears_excess_connections_and_balances_metrics still polls a shared metric every 1 ms. It also relies on the condition total_connections == 1 to mean 'the event was processed', even though run() concurrently executes the immediately scheduled refill.

findings.title: Proxy shutdown handling is inconsistent across the new tests
findings.claim: Proxy shutdown handling is inconsistent across the new tests. keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state matches on proxy.finish() and accepts only DriverDisconnected while the refiller is still alive (drop(refiller) comes after finish). The other new tests drop the refiller first and ignore the result with `let _ = proxy.finish().await`.

findings.title: The comment above start_setting_keyspace_for_connection, 'Requires that the event is for…
findings.claim: The comment above start_setting_keyspace_for_connection, 'Requires that the event is for a successful connection', is now stale. The function takes a Connection, not an event, and its result can now be an Err event.

findings.title: The keyspace-failure arm doesn't check whether the failed USE was for the current keyspace
findings.claim: The keyspace-failure arm doesn't check whether the failed USE was for the current keyspace. A failure for a keyspace that has since been replaced still discards the connection, raises the backoff and can publish a stale Broken error.

findings.title: The keyspace check now runs before sharder/shard-aware-port learning and before the…
findings.claim: The keyspace check now runs before sharder/shard-aware-port learning and before the advanced-shard-awareness mismatch check. If USE fails, a connection that reports a new sharder or port is dropped without the pool learning either. Learning on success now also waits for the USE round trip, which has no timeout.

findings.title: The metrics behavior change in de164845 lands with no test
findings.claim: The metrics behavior change in de164845 lands with no test. Its regression tests arrive only in the separate commit 0d91aa54, so the behavior commit is untested on its own.

findings.title: In commit 0d91aa54, `use futures::FutureExt;` is unconditional, but its only use (`
findings.claim: In commit 0d91aa54, `use futures::FutureExt;` is unconditional, but its only use (`.boxed()`) is inside a `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]` test. That commit therefore produces an unused-import warning when tests are built without `metrics`.

findings.title: The stated validation command does not run the metrics tests or enable the metrics feature
findings.claim: The stated validation command does not run the metrics tests or enable the metrics feature. All metrics assertions in the new keyspace tests are compiled out, and the three tests from 0d91aa54 (including the one fixed in 617139df) are never run.

findings.title: The PR body and title describe only the keyspace fix
findings.claim: The PR body and title describe only the keyspace fix. They omit commits de164845, 0d91aa54 and 617139df, which change the total_connections metric accounting in three clearing paths.

findings.title: The new private enum ConnectionSetupError has a vague, undocumented name that collides…
findings.claim: The new private enum ConnectionSetupError has a vague, undocumented name that collides with the existing public ConnectionSetupRequestError. It mixes two distinct stages: TCP/handshake open failure and post-open USE keyspace failure, which is the pool's 'keyspace parking' step.

findings.title: The public #[from] UseKeyspaceError on ConnectionError adds a permanent From impl to the…
findings.claim: The public #[from] UseKeyspaceError on ConnectionError adds a permanent From impl to the public API. It also places request-level errors, including server DbErrors wrapped in UseKeyspaceError::RequestError, inside the connection-level ConnectionError family that ConnectionPoolError::Broken exposes.
